curve-growth: F(v)=exp[−A φ(v)] with unit-area Gaussian φ, A=5×10^ΔA km/s and sigma=b/√2. W is integrated and converted at a hypothetical 500 nm line. Inversion uses the same fixed transition strength and atmosphere proxy; it returns only a synthetic differential abundance, not a calibrated A(X) or Codex result. This Gaussian-opacity model shows linear and saturation regimes, not the damping-wing branch. Increasing b can increase saturated EW at unchanged abundance. Instrument convolution conserves full EW and is distinct from opacity broadening.
